STUDYQURAN:5:27/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r4.claim: The idiom for stretching hands against someone links the plot against Muhammad in 5:11 with Cain's intent to kill Abel.
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r4.anchor: The idiomatic phrase stretch forth their hands against is also used to describe the intent to kill in the present account

STUDYQURAN:5:27/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r7.speaker: al-Ṭabarī
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r7.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says the story encourages Muslims to treat the Jews who plotted against Muhammad and his followers leniently, following Abel's restraint.
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r7.anchor: Al-Ṭabarī, however, suggests that the reason for telling this story was to encourage the Muslims to deal leniently

STUDYQURAN:5:27/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r8.claim: Al-Ṭabarī cites a hadith telling Muslims to follow the better of Adam's two sons and leave the worse path.
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r8.anchor: Verily God gives you the example of the two sons of Adam; so take [the path of] the better of the two

STUDYQURAN:5:27/r23.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r23.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r23.claim: Commentators debate why Abel refused to oppose Cain or defend himself despite the explicit death threat.
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r23.anchor: Commentators question why Abel refused to oppose his brother’s attack or defend himself

STUDYQURAN:5:27/r24.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r24.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r24.claim: Some say Abel's restraint clarified and emphasized the enormity of his brother's murderous intent and act.
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r24.anchor: Some argue that this was a way of clarifying and emphasizing the enormity of his brother’s murderous intention and action

STUDYQURAN:5:27/r25.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r25.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r25.claim: Others say self-defense against an attacker had not yet been made lawful in early human history.
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r25.anchor: attacking another in self-defense had not been made legitimate at this early stage of human history

STUDYQURAN:5:27/r26.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r26.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r26.claim: Others read Abel's words as rejecting preemptive intent or killing in self-defense, not necessarily all self-defense.
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r26.anchor: is not necessarily an abandonment of self-defense, but an abandonment of the intention to kill his brother preemptively

STUDYQURAN:5:27/r27.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r27.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r27.claim: Some accounts say Cain killed Abel as he slept, leaving him unable to defend himself; this does not establish that he would not have fought while awake.
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r27.anchor: Some accounts indicate that Cain killed Abel while he was sleeping, and Abel was thus unable to defend himself

STUDYQURAN:5:27/r28.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r28.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r28.claim: Another possibility is that Abel judged being killed preferable to killing, even in self-defense.
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r28.anchor: Abel considered it better to be killed than to kill, even in self-defense

STUDYQURAN:5:27/r29.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r29.speaker: al-Qurṭubī
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r29.claim: Al-Qurṭubī says early pious Muslims, including ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, cited Abel when abstaining from violence in the First Civil War; Abel showed strength by sparing a fellow monotheist, even a disobedient one.
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r29.anchor: Al-Qurṭubī notes that the pious and prominent early Muslims who, like ʿAbd Allāḥ ibn ʿUmar, abstained from fighting fellow Muslims

TAB-FULL:v8p328/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p328/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p328/r1.claim: The victim says that if his brother extends his hand to kill him, he will not extend his own hand to kill his brother.
TAB-FULL:v8p328/r1.anchor: {لتقتلني ما أنا بباسط يدي إليك} [المائدة: 28] يقول: " ما أنا بماد يدي إليك

TAB-FULL:v8p328/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p328/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
TAB-FULL:v8p328/r2.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr says the victim was the stronger of the two, but scruple kept him from raising his hand against his brother.
TAB-FULL:v8p328/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو، أنه قال: «وايم الله، إن كان المقتول لأشد الرجلين، ولكن منعه التحرج أن يبسط إلى أخيه»

TAB-FULL:v8p328/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p328/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v8p328/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas glosses the victim’s words as refusing to retaliate and resolving to keep his hand from his brother.
TAB-FULL:v8p328/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {لئن بسطت إلي يدك لتقتلني

TAB-FULL:v8p328/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p328/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v8p328/r4.claim: Mujahid says scripture commanded that a person whom another sought to kill should leave him unresisted.
TAB-FULL:v8p328/r4.anchor: قال مجاهد: كان كتب الله عليهم: إذا أراد الرجل أن يقتل رجلا تركه ولا يمتنع منه

TAB-FULL:v8p328/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p328/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p328/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers that both brothers were forbidden to kill unjustly; the victim’s words express his own refusal to commit the equally forbidden murder. No evidence shows he knew of the threat in time to defend himself; scholars report he was killed asleep, and the verse does not command passivity.
TAB-FULL:v8p328/r5.anchor: وأولى القولين في ذلك بالصواب أن يقال: إن الله عز ذكره قد كان حرم عليهم قتل نفس بغير نفس ظلما، وأن المقتول قال لأخيه

TAB-FULL:v8p328/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p328/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p328/r6.claim: He fears God’s punishment if he extends his hand to kill his brother.
TAB-FULL:v8p328/r6.anchor: وأما تأويل قوله: {إني أخاف الله رب العالمين} [المائدة: 28] فإني أخاف الله في بسط يدي إليك إن بسطتها لقتلك

TAB-FULL:v8p328/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p328/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p328/r7.claim: “Lord of the worlds” means the owner of all creatures, who can punish him for raising his hand to kill.
TAB-FULL:v8p328/r7.anchor: {رب العالمين} [المائدة: 28] يعني: مالك الخلائق كلها أن يعاقبني على بسط يدي إليك

TABATABAI:5:27-32/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32/r4.claim: The victim says acceptance is God's decision, not his own, and the killer is at fault for lacking piety; the victim will not kill his brother because he fears God and will not choose injustice and Hell.
TABATABAI:5:27-32/r4.anchor: وإنما الاجرام من قبل القاتل حيث لم يتق الله فجازاه الله بعدم قبول قربانه

TABATABAI:5:27-32#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#2/r1.claim: The oath lam conditions a threat; extending the hand is a euphemism for taking the steps and using the means of murder.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#2/r1.anchor: اللام للقسم، وبسط اليد إليه كناية عن الأخذ بمقدمات القتل وإعمال أسبابه

TABATABAI:5:27-32#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#2/r2.claim: The nominal negation, participle, emphatic bāʾ, and oath all stress how far the victim is from intending to kill his brother.

TABATABAI:5:27-32#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#2/r3.claim: Fear of God, who requites each sin with its punishment, awakens piety and restrains people from injustice that leads to ruin.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#2/r3.anchor: فإن ذكر المتقين لربهم وهو الله رب العالمين الذي يجازي في كل إثم بما يتعقبه من العذاب

TABATABAI:5:27-32#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#2/r6.claim: The slain brother is shown to be pious by his statement that God accepts only the pious, which God repeats without correction, and knowledgeable of God by his professed fear of Him, likewise affirmed.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#2/r6.anchor: المتضمن لدعوى التقوى، وقد أمضاها الله تعالى بنقله من غير رد

TABATABAI:5:27-32#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#3/r1.claim: By approving the speaker’s declaration of fear, God depicts him as learned; the Qur’an likewise says that only learned servants fear God and calls Moses’ companion learned.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#3/r1.anchor: فحكايته تعالى قوله { إني أخاف الله رب العالمين } وإمضاؤه له توصيف له بالعلم

TABATABAI:5:27-32#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#3/r3.claim: The text does not say he refused to defend himself; he only says he will not kill first, and may have been attacked by surprise, killed while defending himself, or while evading the attack.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#3/r3.anchor: لم يقل لأخيه حينما كلمه إنك إن أردت أن تقتلني ألقيت نفسي بين يديك ولم أدافع عن نفسي

TABATABAI:5:27-32#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#3/r4.claim: His willingness to accept the stated consequence applies only if his brother initiates; it does not mean he desired death to secure his own salvation by damning his brother.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#3/r4.anchor: وإنما قال إني أريد ذلك وأختاره على تقدير بسطك يدك لقتلي

TABATABAI:5:27-32#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#3/r5.speaker: بعض المتقشفين من أهل العبادة والورع
TABATABAI:5:27-32#3/r5.claim: Some ascetics hold that one should passively accept oppression, since the oppressor alone bears its sin; Tabatabai calls this ignorance about complicity in wrongdoing.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#3/r5.anchor: كبعض المتقشفين من أهل العبادة والورع حيث يرى أن الذي عليه هو التزهد والتعبد

TABATABAI:5:27-32#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#3/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#3/r6.claim: Helping another commit sin makes both helper and helped share guilt, so the victim’s alleged passivity cannot be justified by saying only the aggressor bears the wrongdoing.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#3/r6.anchor: فإنه من الإعانة على الإثم، وهي توجب اشتراك المعين والمعان في الإثم جميعا

TABATABAI:5:27-32#15/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#15/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#15/r2.claim: The report's apparent account is that Qabil killed Habil by stealth, without Habil enabling the attack; al-Tabataba'i says this better fits reflection and his prior discussion.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#15/r2.anchor: وظاهرها أن قابيل إنما قتل هابيل غيلة من غير أن يمكنه من نفسه

TABATABAI:5:27-32#16/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#16/r2.speaker: علي بن الحسين
TABATABAI:5:27-32#16/r2.claim: In a report from ʿAli ibn al-Husayn, Habil offered a prized ram and Qabil a sheaf; Satan taught Qabil to smash Habil's head with stones, and a raven taught him burial, after which Adam mourned and received Hibat Allah (Shith).
TABATABAI:5:27-32#16/r2.anchor: علي بن الحسين عليه السلام يحدث رجالا من قريش قال لما قربا ابنا آدم القربان

TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r2.speaker: روايات
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r2.claim: Another report says Habil let Qabil kill him and refrained from raising a hand against his brother.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r2.anchor: والقائلة أن هابيل مكن قابيل من نفسه وانه تحرج ان يبسط يده إلى أخيه

TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r8.speaker: روايات
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r8.claim: Another report claims their law required a person targeted by an attacker to let the attacker do as he wished without resistance.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r8.anchor: والقائلة انه كان من شريعتهم ان الإنسان إذا قصده آخر تركه وما يريد

TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r9.claim: Al-Tabataba'i rejects these and similar reports as mostly or entirely weak, inconsistent with sound reflection and the Qur'an, and likely fabricated, distorted, or corrupted in transmission.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r9.anchor: فهذه وأمثالها روايات من طرق جلها أو كلها ضعيفة

TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r10.speaker: النبي
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r10.claim: A report transmitted from ʿUmar says the Prophet advised someone facing a would-be killer to act like the better son of Adam: the victim is in Paradise and the killer in Hell.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r10.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم " يعجز أحدكم أتاه الرجل أن يقتله

TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r11.speaker: النبي
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r11.claim: A report from Abu Musa tells believers during civil strife to break their swords, cut their bowstrings, stay indoors, and be like the better son of Adam.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r11.anchor: عن البيهقي عن أبي موسى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال " اكسروا سيفكم يعني في الفتنة

TABATABAI:5:27-32#18/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#18/r1.speaker: النبي
TABATABAI:5:27-32#18/r1.claim: A report transmitted by Ibn Jarir and ʿAbd al-Razzaq from al-Hasan says the two sons of Adam exemplify this community, which should follow the better of them.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#18/r1.anchor: عن ابن جرير وعبد الرزاق عن الحسن قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

TABATABAI:5:27-32#18/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#18/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#18/r2.claim: These fitna reports read Habil's statement as surrendering to Qabil and refusing self-defense; al-Tabataba'i rejects that reading because sound reports and Qur'an support defending oneself and truth, including fighting a transgressing faction.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#18/r2.anchor: الآثار الصحيحة الآمرة بالدفاع عن النفس والانتصار للحق

TABATABAI:5:27-32#18/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#18/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#18/r3.claim: Al-Tabataba'i distrusts these narrations because their transmitters included people who sat out the civil strife and ʿAli's wars; they should be reinterpreted if possible, otherwise discarded.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#18/r3.anchor: في حروب علي عليه السلام مع معاوية والخوارج وطلحة والزبير

TABATABAI:5:27-32#18/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#18/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#18/r4.claim: Al-Tabataba'i rejects the reading that Habil enabled Qabil to kill him and left himself undefended.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#18/r4.anchor: بأن المراد تمكين هابيل لأخيه في قتله وتركه الدفاع، وقد عرفت ما فيه

TABATABAI:5:27-32#19/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#19/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#19/r3.claim: Al-Tabataba'i urges readers to compare the Torah's account of the brothers with the Qur'an's account and judge the differences.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#19/r3.anchor: وعليك أن تتدبر ما تشتمل عليه القصة على ما قصتها التوراة وعلى ما قصها القرآن

TABATABAI:5:27-32#20/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#20/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#20/r4.claim: Habil's dialogue conveys innate religious knowledge: monotheism, prophethood, resurrection, piety, injustice, divine law, and God's justice in acceptance and afterlife recompense.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#20/r4.anchor: ثم يذكر محاورة الأخوين فيقص عن المقتول من غرر المعارف الفطرية الإنسانية وأصول المعارف الدينية

TABRISI:5:28-29/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:28-29/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:28-29/r1.claim: Basṭ means extension or spreading out, the opposite of contraction.

TABRISI:5:28-29/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:28-29/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:28-29/r5.claim: The lām in la-in is an oath lām, and its answer is mā anā bi-bāsiṭ; mā cannot be a conditional answer, and the prior oath answer takes precedence.
TABRISI:5:28-29/r5.anchor: لئن بسطت اللام للقسم وجوابه ما أنا بباسط

TABRISI:5:28-29/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:28-29/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:28-29/r6.claim: Hābil answers his brother's threat: if you extend your hand to kill me, I will not extend mine to kill you.
TABRISI:5:28-29/r6.anchor: ثم أخبر سبحانه عن هابيل أنه قال لأخيه حين هدده بالقتل

TABRISI:5:28-29/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:28-29/r7.speaker: الحسن، مجاهد، الجبائي
TABRISI:5:28-29/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Mujāhid, as preferred by al-Jubbāʾī, say defensive killing was not permitted then; Hābil was commanded to endure so God Himself would exact justice.
TABRISI:5:28-29/r7.anchor: القتل على سبيل المدافعة لم يكن مباحا في ذلك الوقت

TABRISI:5:28-29/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:28-29/r8.speaker: ابن عباس وجماعة
TABRISI:5:28-29/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and others say Hābil meant he would not initiate wrongful aggression; they say Qābil murdered him stealthily while he slept by dropping a rock on him.
TABRISI:5:28-29/r8.anchor: على وجه الظلم والابتداء عن ابن عباس وجماعة

TABRISI:5:28-29/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:28-29/r9.speaker: المرتضى
TABRISI:5:28-29/r9.claim: Al-Murtaḍā finds the apparent sense different from both readings: if his brother reaches to kill him, Hābil will not wrong him, since self-defense is permissible to escape harm without intending to kill.

TABRISI:5:28-29/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:28-29/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:28-29/r10.claim: Hābil says he fears God if he stretches his hand to kill his brother.

THALABI:v4p50/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p50/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
THALABI:v4p50/r1.claim: Ibn ʿUmar swears that the murdered brother was the stronger of the two, but scruple kept him from raising his hand against his brother.
THALABI:v4p50/r1.anchor: قال عبد الله بن عمر: أيم الله إن كان المقتول لأشد الرجلين ولكن منعه التحرج أن يبسط إلى أخيه يده

THALABI:v4p50/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p50/r2.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v4p50/r2.claim: Mujahid says that at that time a person threatened with murder was commanded to leave the attacker and not resist.
THALABI:v4p50/r2.anchor: وقال مجاهد: كتب عليهم في ذلك الوقت، إذا أراد رجل قتل رجل أن يتركه ولا يمتنع منه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p337/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p337/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وحذيفة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p337/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and Hudhayfa explain: if you begin by trying to kill me, I will not be the one who begins by killing you.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p337/r1.anchor: وهذا يروى عن ابن عباس (¬2) وحذيفة (¬3).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p337/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p337/r2.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p337/r2.claim: Al-Hasan and Mujahid say it was prescribed for people at that time to let an attacker kill them rather than resist.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p337/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن ومجاهد: إنه كتب عليهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p337/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p337/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p337/r3.claim: A person defending himself must use the least force needed and aim to repel, not kill; if killing the attacker is the only possible defense, it is allowed, though a victim may choose to submit to unjust death.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p337/r3.anchor: وقال أهل العلم: الدافع عن نفسه يدفع بالأيسر فالأيسر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p337/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p337/r4.speaker: عثمان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p337/r4.claim: The source says Uthman acted by submitting rather than killing an unjust attacker.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p337/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p337/r5.speaker: رسول الله
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p337/r5.claim: The Prophet instructed Muhammad ibn Maslama to cover his face with his sleeve and be God's slain servant rather than God's killer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p337/r5.anchor: أمر رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - (¬7) محمد بن مسلمة (¬8)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p337/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p337/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p337/r6.claim: The verse shows that one facing a would-be murderer may not raise a hand with the intention of killing; any action must intend to repel.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p337/r6.anchor: فبان أن بسط اليد لقتل القاصد للقتل لا يجوز

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p337/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p337/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p337/r7.claim: Abd Allah ibn Amr says the slain brother was the stronger man, but scrupulous fear of God kept him from raising his hand against his brother.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p337/r7.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن عمرو في هذه الآية: والله إن كان المقتول لأشد الرجلين

QASHANI:5:28-29/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:5:28-29/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:5:28-29/r1.claim: Intellect will not destroy estimation's useful sensory work or its life through soul and desire, because each has a proper function.
QASHANI:5:28-29/r1.anchor: لأني لا أبطل أعمالك التي هي شديدة في مواضعها من المحسوسات ولا أقطع عنك حياتك التي هي مدد النفس والهوى

QASHANI:5:28-29/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:5:28-29/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:5:28-29/r2.claim: Intellect knows that partial interests, sensory judgments, and arranging livelihood depend on estimation; without its hopes and aspirations, people could not sustain themselves.
QASHANI:5:28-29/r2.anchor: إذ العقل يعلم أن المصالح الجزئية وأحكام المحسوسات والمعاني الجزئية المعلقة بها وترتيب أسباب المعاش كلها لا تحصل

QASHANI:5:28-29/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:5:28-29/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:5:28-29/r3.claim: Qashani cites the verse that only the learned truly fear God to explain Abel's fear as knowledge of God.
QASHANI:5:28-29/r3.anchor: وقال: إنما يخشى الله من عباده العلماء

QASHANI:5:28-29/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:5:28-29/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:5:28-29/r4.claim: Intellect does not interfere with estimation because it knows God created it for a purpose and wisdom.
QASHANI:5:28-29/r4.anchor: واعلم بأنه إنما خلقك لشأن وأوجدك لحكمة، فلا أتعرض له في ذلك

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:27-30/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:27-30/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:27-30/r5.claim: Even if Cain begins to kill him, Abel will not initiate murder because he fears God.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:27-30/r5.anchor: { لئن بسطت إلي يدك } لئن بدأتني بالقتل فما أنا بالذي أبدؤك بالقتل { إني أخاف الله } في قتلك.

ELMALILI:5:27-31/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:27-31/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:27-31/r9.claim: He refuses to raise his hand to kill his brother because he fears God, Lord of all worlds.
ELMALILI:5:27-31/r9.anchor: Çünkü ben, Rabbü’l-âlemîn olan Allah’tan her hâlde korkarım

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:28/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:28/r1.speaker: Mevdûdî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:28/r1.claim: The words mean that Habil would not act first to kill his brother, even after learning of his murderous intent and preparations.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:28/r1.anchor: Mevdûdî, bu sözleri şöyle yorumlar: “Beni öldürmek için kötü niyetler besleyebilirsin; fakat ben, senin beni öldürme hazırlıklarını öğrendikten sonra bile

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:28/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:28/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:28/r2.claim: This does not mean Habil lacked the power to defend himself; he could have killed his attacker, but refrained because taking life is forbidden and among the gravest sins.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:28/r2.anchor: Bu ifade aynı zamanda Hâbil’in kendisini savunup saldırgan kardeşini öldürebilecek güçte olduğunu, fakat cana kıymak haram ve Allah katında en büyük günah

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:28/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:28/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:28/r3.claim: Islam permits self-defense and does not treat surrendering to death as virtuous; virtue lies in not starting an attack, while disabling an attacker is a right and generally a duty.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:28/r3.anchor: İslâm’da nefsi müdafaa meşrû bir haktır, kişinin kendisini ölüme teslim etmesi fazilet olarak kabul edilemez. Fazilet saldırıyı başlatmamaktır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:29/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:29/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:29/r1.claim: In addition to fearing God and not attempting murder, Habil says his brother would bear both sins and go to Hell; this is not a claim that one person is normally liable for another’s sin, since 17:15 says otherwise.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:29/r1.anchor: Önceki âyette Hâbil’in Allah’tan korktuğu için kardeşini öldürme teşebbüsünde bulunmadığı bildirilirken burada ikinci bir sebep olarak kardeşinin her ikisinin günahını yüklenerek cehenneme gitmesini

BURHAN:v3p379/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p379/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p379/r2.claim: Normally, where a verb has a direct object and an oblique object, the direct object precedes the prepositional phrase; the source compares this with the ordering in 48:24.
BURHAN:v3p379/r2.anchor: فإن كان في الكلام مفعولان أحدهما يعدى وصول الفعل إليه بالحرف والآخر بنفسه قدم ما تعدى إليه الفعل بنفسه

BURHAN:v3p379/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p379/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p379/r3.claim: The first clause reverses the ordinary order to avoid a heavy run of nearby articulation points in بسطت ... لتقتلني.
BURHAN:v3p379/r3.anchor: مانع أقوى وهو مخافة أن يتوالى ثلاثة أحرف متقاربات المخرج فيثقل الكلام بسبب ذلك

BURHAN:v3p379/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p379/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p379/r4.claim: The second clause uses an active participle instead of a finite verb to make the comparison apt; with the sound obstacle gone, it follows the usual object order.
BURHAN:v3p379/r4.anchor: لما أمن هذا المحذور في عجز الآية لما اقتضته البلاغة من الإتيان باسم الفاعل موضع الجملة الفعلية

BURHAN:v3p379/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p379/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p379/r5.claim: The word order reflects the contrast: the first brother is eager to aggress and is expressed with a verb, while the other denies aggression and is expressed with a participle.
BURHAN:v3p379/r5.anchor: لما كان الأول حريصا على التعدي على الغير قدم المتعدى على الآلة فقال إلى يدك

ITQAN:v3p56/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p56/r2.speaker: ابن حبيب النيسابوري
ITQAN:v3p56/r2.claim: Ibn Habib al-Nisaburi allows abrogation by Sunna when it comes through revelation commanded by God, but not when it rests on independent reasoning.
ITQAN:v3p56/r2.anchor: حكاه ابن حبيب النيسابوري في تفسيره

ITQAN:v3p56/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p56/r3.speaker: الشافعي
ITQAN:v3p56/r3.claim: Al-Shafi'i says Quran abrogation by Sunna has a supporting Quran text, and Sunna abrogation by Quran has a supporting Sunna, showing their agreement.
ITQAN:v3p56/r3.anchor: وقال الشافعي حيث وقع نسخ القرآن بالسنة فمعها قرآن عاضد لها وحيث وقع نسخ السنة بالقرآن فمعه سنة عاضدة له

ITQAN:v3p56/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p56/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p56/r4.claim: Abrogation applies only to commands and prohibitions, including those phrased as reports; it does not apply to nonprescriptive reports, promises, or threats.
ITQAN:v3p56/r4.anchor: الثالثة لا يقع النسخ إلا في الأمر والنهي ولو بلفظ الخبر أما الخبر الذي ليس بمعنى الطلب فلا يدخله النسخ ومنه الوعد والوعيد

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r1.speaker: author
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r1.claim: Occasions of revelation clarify meaning and ambiguity; the author rejects calling them useless history.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r1.anchor: وأخطأ من قال لا فائدة له لجريانه مجرى التاريخ ومن فوائدة الوقوف على المعني أو إزالة الاشكال

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r2.speaker: الواحدي
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r2.claim: Al-Wahidi says a verse cannot be interpreted without its story and cause of revelation.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r2.anchor: قال الواحدي لا يمكن معرفة تفسير الآية دون الوقوف على قصتها وبيان سبب نزولها

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r3.speaker: ابن دقيق العيد
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r3.claim: Ibn Daqiq al-ʿId calls the cause a strong path to understanding Qur’anic meanings.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r3.anchor: وقال ابن دقيق العيد بيان سبب النزول طريق قوي في فهم معاني القرآن

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r4.speaker: ابن تيميه
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r4.claim: Ibn Taymiyya says knowing a cause aids interpretation because it yields knowledge of what it occasioned; early readers’ ambiguities could thereby be resolved.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r4.anchor: وقال ابن تيميه معرفة سبب النزول يعين على فهم الآية فإن العلم بالسبب يورث العلم بالمسبب

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r5.speaker: عبيده
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r5.claim: Ubayda told Muhammad ibn Sirin to fear God and speak correctly, since those who knew why the Qur’an was revealed had passed away.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r5.anchor: وقد قال محمد بن سيرين سألت عبيده عن آية من القرآن فقال اتق الله وقل سدادا ذهب الذين يعلمون فيم أنزل القرآن

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r6.speaker: الواحدي
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r6.claim: Al-Wahidi permits speaking about causes only through reports from those who witnessed revelation and knew its occasions.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r6.anchor: قال الواحدي ولا يحل القول في أسباب نزول الكتاب إلا بالرواية والسماع ممن شاهدوا التنزيل ووقفوا على الأسباب

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r7.speaker: غيره
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r7.claim: Other authorities say Companions inferred causes from contextual clues and could state an attribution tentatively.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r7.anchor: وقال غيره معرفة سبب النزول أمر يحصل للصحابة بقرائن تحتف بالقضايا وربما لم يجزم بعضهم فقال أحسب هذه الآية نزلت في كذا

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r9.speaker: الحاكم
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r9.claim: Al-Hakim calls a witnessed Companion’s report that a verse was revealed about an event musnad; Ibn al-Salah followed him.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r9.anchor: وقال الحاكم في علوم الحديث إذا أخبر الصحابي الذي شهد الوحي والتنزيل عن آية من القرآن أنها نزلت في كذا فإنه حديث مسند

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r11.speaker: ابن تيمية
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r11.claim: Ibn Taymiyya says ‘revealed about’ can denote either a cause or a case included under the verse despite not causing its revelation.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r11.anchor: وقال ابن تيمية قولهم نزلت الآية في كذا يراد به تارة أنها سبب النزول ويراد به تارة أن ذلك داخل في الآية

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r12.speaker: البخاري
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r12.claim: Al-Bukhari treats a Companion’s ‘revealed about’ statement as musnad.

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r13.speaker: غيره
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r13.claim: Other scholars treat that statement as tafsir, not musnad; most musnads, including Ahmad’s, follow them.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r13.anchor: وغيره لا يدخله فيه وأكثر المسانيد على هذا الإصطلاح كمسند أحمد وغيره

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r14.speaker: author
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r14.claim: All scholars treat an explicitly described precipitating event as musnad.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r14.anchor: بخلاف ما إذا ذكر سببا نزلت عقبه فإنهم كلهم يدخلون مثل هذا في المسند

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r15.speaker: الزركشي
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r15.claim: Al-Zarkashi says ‘revealed about’ usually meant the verse included that ruling, not that the case caused revelation.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r15.anchor: وقال الزركشي في البرهان قد عرف من عادة الصحابة والتابعين أن أحدهم إذا قال نزلت هذه الآية في كذا

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r16.speaker: author
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r16.claim: The author defines an occasion as an event occurring when the verse descended.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r16.anchor: قلت والذي يتحرر في سبب النزول أنه ما نزلت الآية أيام وقوعه

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r19.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r19.speaker: author
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r19.claim: The author directs readers to al-Itqan, section nine, for more examples and discussions omitted here.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p1/r19.anchor: وقد بسطت أمثلة ذلك في النوع التاسع من كتاب الإتقان في علوم القرآن وذكرت له فوائد أخرى من مباحث وتحقيقات لا يحتملها هذا الكتاب

MAJAZ:v1p160/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p160/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p160/r3.claim: Basatta ilayya yadaka means you extended your hand toward me.
MAJAZ:v1p160/r3.anchor: «بسطت إلي يدك» (28) أي مددت. «أن تبوء بإثمي وإثمك» أي أن تحتمل إثمى

MAJAZ:v1p160/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p160/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p160/r4.claim: Tabūʾa bi-ithmī wa-ithmika means to bear my sin and your sin; elsewhere it means to admit a sin, kill someone in retaliation, or arrive at a lodging. ʿAmr b. Ḥunā’s verse illustrates the blood-for-blood usage.
MAJAZ:v1p160/r4.anchor: «أن تبوء بإثمي وإثمك» أي أن تحتمل إثمى وتفوز به، وله موضع آخر: أن تقر به

SAMIN-DURR:5:28/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:28/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:28/r1.claim: The lām in la-in is an oath-introducing lām; the reply answers an omitted oath, following the rule that the earlier of a condition and oath is answered.
SAMIN-DURR:5:28/r1.anchor: واللام في قوله: { لئن }: هي الموطئة

SAMIN-DURR:5:28/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:28/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:5:28/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains that a verbal condition paired with an active participle in the response emphasizes refusal of this heinous act; bāʾ reinforces the negation.
SAMIN-DURR:5:28/r2.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " فإن قلت: لم جاء الشرط بلفظ الفعل، والجزاء بلفظ اسم الفاعل وهو قوله: { لئن بسطت إلي يدك لتقتلني مآ أنا بباسط }؟ قلت: ليفيد

SAMIN-DURR:5:28/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:28/r3.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:5:28/r3.claim: The Shaykh argues that “I am not one who stretches” answers the oath, not the condition; a negated conditional answer would need fa and violate the precedence rule.
SAMIN-DURR:5:28/r3.anchor: قال: " لأن هذا جواب للقسم لا للشرط

SAMIN-DURR:5:28/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:28/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:28/r4.claim: Al-Samīn rejects the criticism: al-Zamakhsharī calls it the condition’s consequence because it expresses that consequence, which is unobjectionable terminology.
SAMIN-DURR:5:28/r4.anchor: وهذا ليس بشيء لأن أبا القاسم سماه جزاء للشرط

SAMIN-DURR:5:28/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:28/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:28/r5.claim: Al-Samīn notes that al-Zamakhsharī elsewhere treated a similar response as answering the oath while standing in for the condition’s answer.
SAMIN-DURR:5:28/r5.anchor: وقد خالف الزمخشري كلامه هنا بما ذكره في البقرة

ZAJJAJ:v2p166/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p166/r6.speaker: يقال
ZAJJAJ:v2p166/r6.claim: It is said that swords were forbidden then, as in Muhammad's Meccan period and in Jesus's time.
ZAJJAJ:v2p166/r6.anchor: ويقال إن السيف كان ممنوعا في ذلك الوقت كما كان حين كان النبي

ZAJJAJ:v2p166/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p166/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p166/r7.claim: The speaker says he will not retaliate, fight, or kill his brother because he fears the Lord of all worlds.
ZAJJAJ:v2p166/r7.anchor: أي: ما أنا بمجازيك ولا مقاتلك، ولا قاتلك:

NASHR:v2p255/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p255/r9.speaker: المدنيان، وأبو عمرو، وحفص
NASHR:v2p255/r9.claim: The two Medinans, Abu Amr, and Hafs open the possessive yāʾ in “يدي إليك.”
NASHR:v2p255/r9.anchor: يدي إليك فتحها المدنيان، وأبو عمرو وحفص

NASHR:v2p255/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p255/r10.speaker: المدنيان، وابن كثير، وأبو عمرو
NASHR:v2p255/r10.claim: The two Medinans, Ibn Kathir, and Abu Amr open the possessive yāʾ in both “إني أخاف” and “لي أن أقول.”
NASHR:v2p255/r10.anchor: إني أخاف، لي أن أقول فتحهما المدنيان، وابن كثير وأبو عمرو

QIRAAT-ER:5:28:12#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:5:28:12#1/r1.speaker: Y-id
QIRAAT-ER:5:28:12#1/r1.claim: The shortened final vowel in yadī contrasts with yadiya, a minor phonetic difference without semantic change.
QIRAAT-ER:5:28:12#1/r1.anchor: Canonical variant: shortened final vowel (yadī instead of yadiya) -- minor phonetic difference, no semantic change

QIRAAT-ER:5:28:16#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:5:28:16#1/r1.speaker: Y-id
QIRAAT-ER:5:28:16#1/r1.claim: An added fatḥa on the final yāʾ lengthens the pronunciation of innī without changing meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:5:28:16#1/r1.anchor: Canonical variant: added fatḥa on final yā' (inniya instead of innī) -- phonetic lengthening variant, no semantic change

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p187#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p187#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p187#2/r3.claim: Qatāda explains the threatened return with both sins as the sin of killing me and your own sin.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p187#2/r3.anchor: وأما قوله ﴿ إني أريد أن تبوء بإثمي وإثمك ﴾ فيقول بإثم قتلي وإثمك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains Abel’s words as saying he would not take revenge for himself.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r5.anchor:
قال ابن عباس:
المعنى ما أنا بمنتصر لنفسي.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r6.speaker: عكرمة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r6.claim: ʿIkrima explains that Abel would not initiate the killing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r6.anchor: وقال عكرمة: المعنى ما كنت لأبتدئك بالقتل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r7.speaker: مجاهد والحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r7.claim: Mujāhid and al-Ḥasan say self-defense was not lawful at that time.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r7.anchor: وقال مجاهد والحسن: لم يكن الدفع عن النفس في ذلك الوقت جائزا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r8.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو وابن عباس والجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r8.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, Ibn ʿAbbās and the majority say Abel was stronger but refrained scrupulously; this implies Cain was sinful, not an unbeliever, since Abel would otherwise have killed him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r8.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن عمرو وابن عباس والجمهور: كان هابيل أشد قوة من قابيل، ولكنه تحرج من القتل،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r9.claim: A comparison says ʿUthmān, promised Paradise despite an ordeal, saw in a dream on the day he was killed that he would break his fast with the Prophet’s company, so he did not defend himself.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r9.anchor: وكما جرى لعثمان إذ بشره الرسول بالجنة على بلوى تصيبه، ورآه في اليوم الذي قتل في النوم وهو يقول:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r10.speaker: النبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r10.claim: A prophetic report tells Abel to turn away and be God’s slain servant rather than God’s killer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r10.anchor: وقال له رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ألق على وجهك وكن عبد الله المقتول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r11.speaker: بعض المفسرين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r11.claim: Another view says Abel saw signs making Cain’s likely attack probable, though not certain, and spoke to deter him and condemn the act; a report says Cain waited until Abel slept and struck him with a large stone.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r11.anchor: وقيل: إن هابيل لاحت له أمارات غلبة الظن من قابيل على قتله، ولكن لم يتحقق ذلك،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r12.speaker: ابن جرير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r12.claim: Ibn Jarīr says the verse does not prove that the victim knew the killer intended to murder him and then left self-defense.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r12.anchor: وقال ابن جرير: ليس في الآية دليل على أن المقتول علم عزل القاتل على قتله،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r13.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r13.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the conditional uses an action while the answer uses a nominal predicate to show Abel will not acquire the vile quality, reinforced by the emphatic bāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p229/r13.anchor: قال الزمخشري: (فإن قلت) : لم جاء الشرط بلفظ الفعل والجزاء بلفظ اسم الفاعل،

ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r1.claim: One account says Habil was stronger but refrained from killing his brother out of fear of God and submitted, because resistance was forbidden under that law.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r1.anchor: قيل كان هابيل أقوى منه ولكن تحرج عن قتله واستسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r2.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the Israelites had been commanded that a person whose life another sought must not resist until the attacker killed him or desisted.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن جريج قال : كانت بنو إسرائيل قد كتب عليهم إذا الرجل بسط يده

ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r3.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r3.claim: Another explanation is that Habil chose the greater reward of being killed rather than killing, assuming self-defense was allowed then.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r3.anchor: أو تحريا لما هو الأفضل الأكثر ثوابا وهو كونه مقتولا لا قاتلا

ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r4.speaker: الجصاص
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r4.claim: Al-Jassas states that the sound legal position now obligates a person to prevent aggression against himself and others, even if doing so results in death.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r4.anchor: فالصحيح من المذهب أنه يلزم الرجل دفع الفساد عن نفسه وغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and others understand Habil to mean that if Qabil initiates unjust aggression, Habil will not initiate aggression in return.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r5.anchor: ولذا قال ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما وغيره : إن المعنى فى الآية

ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r6.claim: On Mujahid's and Ibn Jurayj's interpretation, the verse may be abrogated; whether that happened before the present religious law is disputed.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r6.anchor: وتكون الآية على ماقاله مجاهد وابن جريج : منسوخة وهل نسخت قبل شريعتنا

ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r7.claim: The obligation to oppose aggression is supported by the command to fight the party that transgresses until it returns, along with other verses and hadith.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r7.anchor: والدليل عليه قوله تعالى : فقاتلوا التى تبغى حتى تفىء وغيره من الآيات

ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r8.claim: Another legal view says defense is not obligatory but is permissible.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r8.anchor: وقيل إنه لايلزم ذلك بل يجوز

ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r9.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r9.claim: A report from the Prophet about civil strife says each step toward conflict is worse, and if it comes, one should be killed rather than become the killer; it supports avoiding such fighting.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r9.anchor: عن خباب بن الارت عنه ( صلى الله عليه وسلم ) أنه ذكر فتنة القاعد فيها خير

ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r10.claim: The hadith that both the killer and killed Muslim are in Hell is understood to concern two people who each intended to kill the other, even if they did not fight.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r10.anchor: وأما من منع ذلك الآن مستدلا بحديث إذا التقى المسلمان بسيفيهما

ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r11.speaker: السيد المرتضى
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r11.claim: Al-Sayyid al-Murtada says this is outside the dispute: the purpose-lam marks intended killing, which is blameworthy in every era, unlike defensive action aimed only at escape.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r11.anchor: وعن السيد المرتضى أن الآية ليست من محل النزاع لأن اللام الداخلة

ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r12.claim: The emphatic negation says Habil is not one to extend a hand against Qabil, repudiating even the preliminaries of killing rather than merely saying he would not kill.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r12.anchor: للمبالغة فى أنه ليس من شأنه ذلك ولا ممن يتصف به ولذلك أكد النفى

ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r13.claim: Saying he is not one to extend his hand, rather than simply saying he is not a killer, disavows the steps leading to murder.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r13.anchor: ولم يقل وما أنا بقاتل بل قال : بباسط للتبرى عن مقدمات القتل

ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r14.claim: Fronting the phrase toward me signals from the outset that the harm and consequences of aggression return to its perpetrator.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r14.anchor: وقدم الجار والمجرور المتعلق ببسطت إيذانا على ماقيل من أول الأمر برجوع ضرر

ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r15.claim: The author also suggests that the fronting promptly reminds Qabil of himself and then of their brotherhood, which should prevent murder.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p112#2/r15.anchor: ويحطر لى أنه قدم لتعجيل تذكيره بنفسه المنجر إلى تذكيره بالأخوة

ALUSI-FULL:v6p113/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p113/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p113/r1.claim: Fear of God explains Habil's refusal to raise his hand; it guides Qabil to fear God and implies that a killer does not fear Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p113/r1.anchor: تعليل للامتناع عن بسط يده لقتله وفيه إرشاد قابيل إلى خشية الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43/r1.claim: بسطت means you extended or stretched your hand.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43/r2.claim: Ibn Umar says the victim was the stronger of the two men, but scrupulous fear kept him from raising his hand against his brother.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43/r2.anchor: قال عبد الله بن عمر: وايم الله إن كان المقتول لأشد الرجلين ولكن منعه التحرج أن يبسط إلى أخيه يده،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43/r3.claim: Under Adam’s law, a person threatened with murder could submit and endure to seek reward; the author compares this to Uthman.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43/r3.anchor: وهذا في الشرع آدم جائز لمن أريد قتله أن ينقاد ويستسلم طلبا للأجر كما فعل عثمان رضي الله عنه،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43/r4.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43/r4.claim: Mujahid says they were commanded at that time not to resist if someone intended to kill them, but to be patient.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43/r4.anchor: قال مجاهد: كتب عليهم في ذلك الوقت إذا أراد رجل قتل رجل أن لا يمتنع ويصبر.

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27-28/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27-28/r4.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27-28/r4.claim: Although Abel was stronger, he refrained from killing and submitted out of fear of God, because self-defense was not yet permitted, or because this was the better course.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27-28/r4.anchor: قيل: كان هابيل أقوى منه ولكن تحرج عن قتله واستسلم له خوفا من الله سبحانه وتعالى لأن الدفع لم يبح بعد، أو تحريا لما هو الأفضل

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27-28/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27-28/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27-28/r5.claim: A Prophetic saying advises being God’s slain servant rather than His slayer.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27-28/r5.anchor:
قال عليه الصلاة والسلام:
" كن عبد الله المقتول

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27-28/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27-28/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27-28/r6.claim: Abel disavows the killing altogether to avoid being described by that shameful act; the prefixed bāʾ reinforces the negation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:27-28/r6.anchor: وإنما قال: { ما أنا بباسط } في جواب { لئن بسطت }

BIQAI-FULL:v2p445/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p445/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p445/r5.claim: Abel first admonishes Cain, then explains that fear of God restrains him from defending himself lest resistance carry him beyond permitted bounds; Cain is sinful, not an idolater.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p445/r5.anchor: أعلمه ثانيا أن الخوف من الله منعه من أن يمانعه عن نفسه ملينا لقلبه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p445/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p445/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p445/r6.claim: Abel frames his grave assertion with an emphatic conditional oath because such a serious statement is difficult to believe.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p445/r6.anchor: مؤكدا بالقسم لأن مثل ما يخبر به عظيم لا يكاد يصدق

BIQAI-FULL:v2p445/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p445/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p445/r7.claim: The emphatic negation and fronted object generalize his refusal; the nominal construction avoids asserting certainty about his future conduct, as an act of reverence toward God.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p445/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p445/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p445/r8.claim: Abel’s fear means recalling God’s perfection; calling Him Lord of the worlds recalls His beneficence in creating and nurturing, so Abel will not destroy what God built.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p445/r8.anchor: ثم وصفه بالإحسان إلى خلقه ليكون ذلك مانعا له من الإساءة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p445/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p445/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p445/r9.claim: The author compares Abel’s refusal to resist with ʿUthmān’s similar conduct.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p445/r9.anchor: وهذا كما فعل عثمان رضي الله عنه

DURR-FULL:v3p54/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p54/r3.speaker: ناس من الصحابة
DURR-FULL:v3p54/r3.claim: Cain threatened Abel over the marriage; Abel answered that God accepts only from the God-fearing and wanted Cain to bear the sin of killing him together with his own existing sin.
DURR-FULL:v3p54/r3.anchor: فغضب وقال: لأقتلنك حتى لا تنكح أختي فقال هابيل {إنما يتقبل الله من المتقين}

DURR-FULL:v3p55/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p55/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p55/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says offerings were made before there were poor people to receive charity: a shepherd offered his best sheep and a farmer some crops; fire accepted the sheep, and Cain threatened Abel because people knew whose offering was rejected.
DURR-FULL:v3p55/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان من شأن ابني آدم أنه لم يكن مسكين يتصدق عليه

DURR-FULL:v3p57/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p57/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v3p57/r4.claim: Mujahid says the people addressed had been commanded that if a man wanted to kill another, the victim must let him act and not resist.
DURR-FULL:v3p57/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {لئن بسطت إلي يدك}

DURR-FULL:v3p57/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p57/r5.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v3p57/r5.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the Children of Israel were commanded not to resist when one person raised a hand to kill another, but to let the attacker kill or desist.
DURR-FULL:v3p57/r5.anchor: عن ابن جريج في الآية قال: كانت بنو إسرائيل كتب عليهم

DURR-FULL:v3p57/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p57/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v3p57/r6.claim: Mujahid says the brother's sin that Abel wants him to bear is the sin of killing Abel; his own sin is what he had committed beforehand. Qatada and al-Dahhak report the same explanation.
DURR-FULL:v3p57/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {إني أريد أن تبوء بإثمي وإثمك} قال: بقتلك إياي

DURR-FULL:v3p57/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p57/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p57/r8.claim: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas reports the Prophet's advice during future civil strife: the seated person is safer than the standing, walking, or running person; if an attacker enters one's home, be like Adam's son. Al-Tirmidhi grades it good and al-Hakim authenticates it.
DURR-FULL:v3p57/r8.anchor: عن سعد بن أبي وقاص: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: إنها ستكون فتنة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p138/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p138/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p138/r3.claim: Bast al-yad is figurative for violence or force, as in the threat to extend hands and tongues against people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p138/r3.anchor: وبسط اليد مجاز في البطش قال تعالى : { ويبسطوا إليكم أيديهم وألسنتهم بالسوء }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p138/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p138/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p138/r4.claim: The same expression can figuratively mean having authority or power over others, or being generous, as in the verse about God’s outstretched hands.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p138/r4.anchor: كما في قوله تعالى : { بل يداه مبسوطتان }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p138/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p138/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p138/r5.claim: In the sons of Adam passage, extending a hand is literal: an attempt to seize or grasp someone.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p138/r5.anchor: وهو حقيقة في محاولة الإمساك بشيء ، كما في قوله تعالى حكاية عن ابن آدم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p138/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p138/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p138/r6.claim: Kaff al-yad, “withholding the hand,” is a metaphor for turning away specifically from evil.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p138/r6.anchor: وأما كف اليد فهو مجاز عن الإعراض عن السوء خاصة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p170/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p170/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p170/r1.claim: Habil’s words warn his brother about the gravity of murder and imply he could defend himself but refrains out of fear of God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p170/r1.anchor: وقوله : { لئن بسطت إلي يدك لتقتلني } الخ موعظة لأخيه ليذكره خطر هذا الجرم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p170/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p170/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p170/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAshur’s apparent reading is Habil’s own judgment that even killing in self-defense was a grave offense; he knew what killing meant from slaughter and hunting, and regarded life as sacred even for an unjust person.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p170/r2.anchor: والظاهر أن هذا اجتهاد من هابيل في استعظام جرم قتل النفس ، ولو كان القتل دفاعا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p170/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p170/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p170/r3.claim: Alternatively, the brothers may have learned from Adam a charge to preserve every life, great or small, even when defending oneself.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p170/r3.anchor: ويمكن أن يكونا تلقيا من أبيهما الوصاية بحفظ النفوس صغيرها وكبيرها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p170/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p170/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p170/r4.claim: His fear of God suggests their law prohibited defense that caused the aggressor’s death; Ibn ʿAshur says this was abrogated, since later laws permit necessary self-defense without exceeding what is needed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p170/r4.anchor: فقوله : { إني أخاف الله } يدل على أن الدفاع بما يفضي إلى القتل كان محرما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p170/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p170/r5.speaker: رسول الله
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p170/r5.claim: The hadith about two Muslims meeting with swords is about political conflict and struggle for dominance, where an attacker would stop if the other yielded, rather than a general prohibition on self-defense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p170/r5.anchor: وأما حديث ( إذا التقى المسلمان بسيفيهما فالقاتل والمقتول في النار ) فذلك في القتال على الملك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p170/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p170/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p170/r6.claim: To avoid civil strife, the Prophet ordered the better party to yield and bear the blame; ʿUthman took that position in hope of reconciliation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p170/r6.anchor: فأمر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أصلح الفريقين بالتسليم للآخر وحمل التبعة عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p170/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p170/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p170/r8.claim: The clause explains the preceding refusal; it is set apart and begins with inna to signal the causal force of the explanation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p170/r8.anchor: فالجملة تعليل للتي قبلها ، ولذلك فصلت وافتتحت ب ( إن ) المشعرة بالتعليل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p69/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p69/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p69/r1.claim: A story may be narrated selectively to suit its audience and purpose; different audiences and situations receive different portions, with length adjusted to context.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p69/r1.anchor: سامعيها ، ومن أجل ذلك تجد ذكرا لبعض القصة في موضع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p69/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p69/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p69/r2.claim: The call of Moses is expanded in Ta Ha and al-Shuara but condensed into two verses in al-Furqan, illustrating variation by rhetorical context.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p69/r2.anchor: ألا ترى قصة بعث موسى كيف بسطت في سورة طه ، وسورة الشعراء . وكيف أوجزت في آيتين في سورة الفرقان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p69/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p69/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p69/r3.claim: Some retellings correct an audience's mistaken version of a story, while others do not; Ibn Ashur says these insights may be implicit rather than explicit in earlier scholarship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p69/r3.anchor: ومنها أنه قد يقصد تارة التنبيه على خطأ المخاطبين فيما ينقلونه من تلك القصة ، وتارة لا يقصد ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178#2/r3.claim: Mujahid says people at that time were commanded neither to draw a sword nor to resist someone who sought to kill them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178#2/r3.anchor: فقال مجاهد: كان الفرض عليهم حينئذ أن لا يسل أحد سيفا وأن لا يمتنع من أريد قتله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178#2/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو وجمهور الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178#2/r4.claim: Abdullah ibn Amr and the majority say Abel was stronger than Cain but refrained scrupulously.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178#2/r4.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن عمرو وجمهور الناس: كان هابيل أشد قوة من قابيل، ولكنه تحرج

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178#2/r5.claim: Ibn Atiyya prefers the strength-and-scruple view: Abel's restraint suggests Cain was a sinner rather than an unbeliever, since scruple would make no sense otherwise; the scrupulous person accepts oppression for afterlife reward, as Uthman did.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p178#2/r5.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد رضي الله عنه: وهذا هو الأظهر. ومن هنا يقوى أن قابيل إنما هو عاص لا كافر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p334/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p334/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p334/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas understands the statement as meaning that the speaker would not retaliate to defend himself.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p334/r1.anchor: أحدهما ما أنا بمنتصر لنفسي قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p334/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p334/r2.speaker: عكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p334/r2.claim: Ikrima understands it to mean that the speaker would not initiate the attack.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p334/r2.anchor: والثاني ما كنت لأبتدئك قاله عكرمة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p334/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p334/r3.speaker: ابن عمر وابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p334/r3.claim: Ibn Umar and Ibn Abbas say scruple kept him from defending himself, although he could do so and self-defense was permitted.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p334/r3.anchor: أحدهما أنه منعه التحرج مع قدرته على الدفع وجوازه له قاله ابن عمر وابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p334/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p334/r4.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p334/r4.claim: Al-Hasan and Mujahid say defending oneself was not lawful at that time.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p334/r4.anchor: والثاني أن دفع الإنسان عن نفسه لم يكن في ذلك الوقت جائزا قاله الحسن ومجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p334/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p334/r5.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p334/r5.claim: Ibn Jarir says the verse does not prove the victim knew the murderer's intention and chose not to defend himself; reports say he was killed treacherously, so the text alone cannot establish that claim.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p334/r5.anchor: وقال ابن جرير ليس في الآية دليل على أن المقتول علم عزم القاتل على قتله ثم ترك الدفع عن نفسه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p83/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p83/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p83/r2.claim: ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAmr says the shepherd offered his best, fattest sheep willingly while the farmer offered spoiled grain unwillingly; the accepted sacrifice led to the quarrel, and the murdered brother was stronger but restrained by scruple.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p83/r2.anchor: عن أبي المغيرة، عن عبد الله بن عمرو (4) قال: إن ابني آدم اللذين قربا قربانا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85#2/r1.claim: The righteous brother will not answer his brother’s evil deed in kind, lest both become equal in sin; he fears God, so he patiently bears it and seeks reward.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85#2/r1.anchor: لا أقابلك على صنيعك الفاسد بمثله، فأكون أنا وأنت سواء في الخطيئة،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85#2/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85#2/r2.claim: Abdullah ibn Amr says Abel was the stronger of the two men, but scrupulous piety restrained him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85#2/r2.anchor: قال عبد الله بن عمرو: وايم الله، إن كان لأشد الرجلين ولكن منعه التحرج، يعني الورع.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85#2/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85#2/r3.claim: In a report in both Sahihs, the Prophet says that when two Muslims confront each other with swords, both killer and killed are in Hell because the killed man intended to kill his companion.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85#2/r3.anchor: ولهذا ثبت في الصحيحين، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: "إذا تواجه المسلمان بسيفيهما، فالقاتل والمقتول في النار".

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85#2/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85#2/r4.claim: Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas reports the Prophet’s counsel during civil strife: inaction is safer, and if an attacker comes to kill one at home, be like Adam’s son; al-Tirmidhi grades this report hasan and cites parallel transmitters.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85#2/r4.anchor: أن سعد بن أبي وقاص قال عند فتنة عثمان: أشهد أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إنها ستكون فتنة، القاعد فيها خير من القائم،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85#2/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85#2/r5.claim: In Abu Dawud’s version, Saʿd asks what to do if an assailant enters his home; the Prophet says to be like Adam’s son and recites this verse. Ibn Asakir identifies the additional transmitter as Husayn al-Ashjaʿi.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p85#2/r5.anchor: عن حسين (8) بن عبد الرحمن الأشجعي؛ أنه سمع سعد بن أبي وقاص، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في هذا الحديث قال: فقلت:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p86/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p86/r1.speaker: أيوب السختياني
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p86/r1.claim: Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani says Uthman was the first in this community to act on the verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p86/r1.anchor: قال أيوب السختياني: إن أول من أخذ بهذه الآية من هذه الأمة:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p86/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p86/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p86/r2.claim: Abu Dharr reports the Prophet’s advice for severe famine, death, and bloodshed: show restraint, be patient, stay home, and do not take part in fighting; if forced among a group, do not take up arms, and cover the face from a sword so the assailant bears the sin.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p86/r2.anchor: عن أبي ذر قال: ركب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حمارا وأردفني خلفه، وقال: "يا أبا ذر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p86/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p86/r3.speaker: أبو داود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p86/r3.claim: Muslim and Sunan compilers except al-Nasaʾi transmit Abu Dharr’s report; Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah also give a similar route through al-Mushaʿath, whom Abu Dawud says no one else mentions in this report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p86/r3.anchor: قال أبو داود: ولم يذكر المشعث (9) في هذا الحديث غير حماد بن زيد.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p86/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p86/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p86/r4.claim: At Hudhayfa’s funeral, a man quoted the Prophet saying that in fighting he would retreat into his house and, if attacked, tell the assailant to take his sin and the speaker’s, becoming like the better of Adam’s two sons.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p86/r4.anchor: عن ربعي قال: كنا في جنازة حذيفة، فسمعت رجلا يقول: سمعت هذا يقول في ناس:

JISHUMI:v3p1932/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1932/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p1932/r5.claim: Bast is extension, the opposite of contraction, as spreading is opposite to folding.
JISHUMI:v3p1932/r5.anchor: والبسط: المد المنافي للقبض، وهما نقيضان كالنشر والطي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p658/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p658/r4.speaker: مجاهد
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p658/r4.claim: Mujāhid and others say Abel was stronger but refrained and surrendered from fear of God, since self-defense was not permitted under that law.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p658/r4.anchor: قيل كان أقوى من القاتل وأبطش منه ولكنه تحرج عن قتل أخيه واستسلم له خوفا من الله لأن الدفع لم يكن مباحا في ذلك الوقت قاله مجاهد وغيره

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p659/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p659/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p659/r2.claim: The conditional uses a verb but its answer uses a nominal participle to convey that Abel will not do an act that earns the vile description; the bāʾ reinforces the negation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p659/r2.anchor: ليفيد انه لا يفعل ما يكتسب به هذا الوصف الشنيع ولذلك أكده بالباء المؤكدة للنفي

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p29/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p29/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p29/r1.claim: Abel means that if Cain starts the killing, Abel will not initiate the same against him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p29/r1.anchor: معناه لئن بدأتني بالقتل لم أبدأك بمثله

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p29/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p29/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p29/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ibn Umar say Abel refrained from defending himself out of scruple, despite having the ability and legal permission.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p29/r2.anchor: أحدهما : منعه منه التحرج مع قدرته عليه وجوازه له , وهذا قول ابن عباس , وعبد الله بن عمر .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p29/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p29/r3.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p29/r3.claim: Mujahid and al-Hasan instead say Abel was not permitted to resist the person who intended to kill him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p29/r3.anchor: والثاني : أنه لم يكن له الامتناع ممن أراد إذ ذاك , وهذا قول مجاهد والحسن .

MUQATIL:5:28-31/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:5:28-31/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:5:28-31/r1.claim: Habil says he will not raise his hand to kill his brother because he fears God, Lord of the worlds.
MUQATIL:5:28-31/r1.anchor: قال: وكان هابيل قال لأخيه قابيل: { لئن بسطت إلي يدك لتقتلني... }

NASAFI-FULL:v1p279/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p279/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p279/r1.claim: «Basaṭta» means you extended; «bāsiṭ» means one extending.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p279/r1.anchor: ﴿ لئن بسطت ﴾ مددت ﴿ إلي يدك لتقتلني

NASAFI-FULL:v1p279/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p279/r2.speaker: مدنى وأبو عمرو وحفص
NASAFI-FULL:v1p279/r2.claim: The Medinan reader, Abū ʿAmr, and Ḥafṣ read the form «yadiya».
NASAFI-FULL:v1p279/r2.anchor: يدي ﴾ مدنى و أبو عمرو وحفص ﴿ إليك

NASAFI-FULL:v1p279/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p279/r3.speaker: حجازى وأبو عمرو
NASAFI-FULL:v1p279/r3.claim: The Hijazis and Abū ʿAmr read the reported form «innī akhāfu».
NASAFI-FULL:v1p279/r3.anchor: إنى أخاف حجازى و أبو عمرو

NASAFI-FULL:v1p279/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p279/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p279/r4.claim: One view says Hābīl was stronger but scrupled to kill his brother and surrendered out of fear of God, since defense was not permitted then.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p279/r4.anchor: قيل كان أقوى من القاتل وأبطش منه ولكن تحرج عن قتل اخيه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p279/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p279/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p279/r5.claim: Another view says refraining from defense was obligatory because it would destroy his own life and make him share the killer’s sin; Qābīl attacked treacherously while he was unaware.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p279/r5.anchor: وقيل بل كان ذلك واجبا فإن فيه إهلاك نفسه ومشاركة للقاتل فى اثمه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p279/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p279/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p279/r6.claim: Hābīl’s stated reason for not killing his brother is fear of God.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p279/r6.anchor: و إنما قتله فتكا على غفلة منه

BURSEVI:v2p304/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p304/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p304/r8.claim: Abel says that even if Cain reaches out to kill him, Abel will not do the same in return.
BURSEVI:v2p304/r8.anchor: ما أنا بفاعل مثله لك في وقت من الأوقات ثم علل ذلك بقوله

BURSEVI:v2p304/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p304/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p304/r9.claim: One account says Abel was physically stronger but refrained from killing his brother and submitted out of fear of God because defensive killing was not permitted then.
BURSEVI:v2p304/r9.anchor: قيل كان هابيل أقوى ولكن تحرج عن قتله واستسلم له خوفا من الله تعالى لأن القتل للدفع لم يكن مباحا في ذلك الوقت

BURSEVI:v2p304/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p304/r10.speaker: البغوي
BURSEVI:v2p304/r10.claim: Al-Baghawi says Islamic law allows a person targeted for killing to submit and yield in hope of reward, as Uthman did.
BURSEVI:v2p304/r10.anchor: قال البغوي : وفي الشرع جائز لمن أريد قتله أن ينقاد ويستسلم طلبا للأجر كما فعل عثمان رضي الله عنه

QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r1.claim: Abel means that even if Cain intends to kill him, Abel will not intend to kill Cain; this is his submission.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r1.anchor: أي لئن قصدت قتلي فأنا لا أقصد قتلك فهذا استسلام منه

QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r2.claim: The Prophet advised Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, if a man entered his house and raised his hand to kill him, to be like the better of Adam’s two sons and recited this verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r2.anchor: وروى أبو داود " عن سعد بن أبي وقاص قال قلت يا رسول الله: إن دخل علي بيتي وبسط يده إلي ليقتلني

QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r3.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r3.claim: Mujāhid says the law at that time required people neither to draw a sword nor defend themselves from someone seeking to kill them.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r3.anchor: قال مجاهد: كان الفرض عليهم حينئذ ألا يستل أحد سيفا، وألا يمتنع ممن يريد قتله.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r4.speaker: علمائنا
QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r4.claim: The scholars say such restraint could have been prescribed earlier; Islamic law unanimously permits defense, and the sounder view makes it obligatory to prevent wrongdoing.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r4.anchor: قال علمائنا: وذلك مما يجوز ورود التعبد به، إلا أن في شرعنا يجوز دفعه إجماعا.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r5.speaker: الحشوية
QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r5.claim: The Ḥashwiyya deny that a person under attack may defend himself and cite a report from Abū Dharr.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r5.anchor: وفي الحشوية قوم لا يجوزون للمصول عليه الدفع واحتجوا بحديث أبي ذر،

QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r6.speaker: العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r6.claim: Scholars interpret the Abū Dharr report as requiring restraint amid civil strife and uncertainty, as discussed in al-Tadhkira.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r6.anchor: وحمله العلماء على ترك القتال في الفتنة، وكف اليد عند الشبهة على ما بيناه

QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r7.speaker: عبدالله بن عمرو وجمهور الناس
QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r7.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr and most people say Abel was physically stronger than Cain but refrained from fighting.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r7.anchor: وقال عبدالله بن عمرو وجمهور الناس: كان هابيل أشد قوة من قابيل ولكنه تحرج.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r8.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls this the likeliest reading and says it supports Cain being sinful rather than an unbeliever: Abel scrupled to fight a monotheist and accepted injustice for afterlife reward, like ʿUthmān.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r8.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وهذا هو الأظهر، ومن ها هنا يقوى أن قابيل إنما هو عاص لا كافر

QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r9.claim: Another interpretation is that Abel intended self-defense; a report says he was asleep when Cain crushed his head, and defense against an aggressor is permitted even if it kills him.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r9.anchor: وقيل: المعنى لا أقصد قتلك بل أقصد الدفع عن نفسي، وعلى هذا قيل: كان نائما

QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r10.claim: Another view takes Abel to mean that if Cain starts killing him, Abel will not initiate killing.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r10.anchor: وقيل: لئن بدأت بقتلي فلا أبدأ بالقتل.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r11.claim: Another explanation is that even if Cain attacks unjustly, Abel will not act unjustly because he fears God.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:28-29/r11.anchor: وقيل: أراد لئن بسطت إلي يدك ظلما فما أنا بظالم إني أخاف الله رب العالمين.

RAZI-FULL:v11p162#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p162#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p162#3/r1.claim: Razi asks why Abel did not defend himself even if defense was obligatory or at least lawful; he answers that Abel addressed Cain before the attack to admonish him and deter intentional murder.
RAZI-FULL:v11p162#3/r1.anchor: هذا الكلام على سبيل الوعظ والنصيحة

RAZI-FULL:v11p162#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p162#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p162#3/r2.claim: A report says Cain waited until Abel slept, then killed him by striking his head with a large stone.
RAZI-FULL:v11p162#3/r2.anchor: ولهذا يروى أن قابيل صبر حتى نام هابيل فضرب رأسه بحجر كبير فقتله

RAZI-FULL:v11p162#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p162#3/r3.speaker: أهل العلم
RAZI-FULL:v11p162#3/r3.claim: Scholars say a defender must use the least force necessary and intend to repel the attack, not to kill; killing is permitted only if no lesser defense succeeds.
RAZI-FULL:v11p162#3/r3.anchor: وقال أهل العلم : الدافع عن نفسه يجب عليه أن يدفع

RAZI-FULL:v11p162#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p162#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p162#3/r4.claim: Some say a person may choose to submit to being killed; Uthman did so, and the Prophet told Muhammad ibn Maslama to cover his face and be killed rather than kill.
RAZI-FULL:v11p162#3/r4.anchor: قال بعضهم : المقصود بالقتل إن أراد أن يستسلم جاز له ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v11p162#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p162#3/r5.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v11p162#3/r5.claim: The Prophet's instruction to Muhammad ibn Maslama was: cover your face, be God's slain servant, and do not be God's killing servant.
RAZI-FULL:v11p162#3/r5.anchor: ألق كمك على وجهك وكن عبد الله المقتول ولا تكن عبد الله القاتل

RAZI-FULL:v11p162#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p162#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p162#3/r6.claim: The duty to defend oneself may differ across religious laws; Mujahid says self-defense was not permitted in that era.
RAZI-FULL:v11p162#3/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد : ءن الدفع عن النفس ما كان مباحا

RAZI-FULL:v11p162#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p162#3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p162#3/r7.claim: The conditional uses a verb but the response uses the active participle, stressing that Abel would not acquire the shameful identity of a killer; the prefixed bā reinforces the negation.
RAZI-FULL:v11p162#3/r7.anchor: والجواب : ليفيد أنه لا يفعل ما يكتسب به هذا الوصف الشنيع
